body.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
body.justification: This supporting result validates agreement with the anchor formulas on their regular domain and records the singular and boundary domains handled by the atlas.
body.gap: The 2026 anchor supplies regular inversion formulas but does not state a full-fiber decision procedure on singular support faces or residual-forest boundary strata.
body.consumer: Users of the anchor formulas can verify numerical agreement on regular tables and obtain a defined certification workflow when regular inversions are unavailable.

obligation.what_is_open: Universal coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global structural atlas.
obligation.obstruction: The published regular formula agrees with the cycle target, and the explicit forced-zero rank-two datum is certified, but the universal boundary clause is equivalent to exhaustiveness of the unresolved mixed-support chart list.
obligation.attempted: Matched the published regular PN/PS functional to the cycle target through the established lift, isolated the certified forced-zero boundary branch, and applied the residual-forest theorem to the conditional design-B margin problem.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair computed by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki on their regular domain.  The cited regular-identification result gives, for every compatible SCM satisfying their Conditions 1--3,
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p).
\]
The established cycle-to-SCM lift gives \(\tau(\vartheta)=\tau_C(b,a)\), so every compatible cycle point covered by those conditions has the same value \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\).  Hence any rigid atlas value on that regular domain must agree with the published formula.  Separately, the established explicit boundary theorem proves for the forced-zero datum
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\},
\]
and the established residual-forest theorem exactly eliminates design-B margins conditional on each proposed cycle chart.  These facts verify regular-domain agreement and the displayed boundary branch, but not the assertion that the same structural chart list exhausts every singular or boundary observable law.
